Subject: Accommodation Request for HIST 150 Recorded Lectures

Dear [Student's Name],

I hope this email finds you well. I am writing to address your concern regarding the recorded lectures for HIST 150, which do not have captions. I understand the importance of accessibility for students with disabilities, and I want to assure you that we take this matter seriously.

As you have already established accommodations on file, I would like to inform you that we will work to provide alternative arrangements for the recorded lectures. Our standard protocol for providing captions for recorded lectures is to ensure that all multimedia content, including video and audio recordings, is captioned within 72 hours of the original recording date.

In this case, I have escalated your request to our Accessibility Services team, who will work with the course instructor to provide captions for the recorded lectures. You can expect to receive an update on the status of this request within the next 48 hours.

In the meantime, I would like to offer you the following options:

1. Request a live captioned lecture: If possible, we can arrange for a live captioned lecture for the next scheduled recording session. Please let me know if this is something you would be interested in, and I will work with the instructor to make this arrangement.
2. Alternative format: We can provide an alternative format for the recorded lectures, such as a written transcript or a video with captions. Please let me know if this would be a suitable option for you.

If you have any further questions or concerns, please do not hesitate to reach out to me directly. I am committed to ensuring that you have equal access to the course materials and can succeed in your studies.

Thank you for bringing this matter to my attention, and I look forward to hearing from you soon.

Academic Support Services

Subject: Accessibility Accommodations for Nursing Course Readings

Unfortunately, the scanned images in your nursing course readings may not meet this standard.

I have spoken with our Disability Services office, and they have informed me that we can provide alternative formats for the readings. We will work with the instructor to obtain the readings in a format that is compatible with your screen reader. This may involve scanning the documents again or providing a digital version of the readings.

In the meantime, I would like to request that you please provide me with your screen reader software and any relevant documentation from your disability services provider. This information will help us to expedite the process of obtaining the alternative formats.

Additionally, I would like to schedule a meeting with you and the instructor to discuss possible accommodations for the course. This will ensure that we can provide the necessary support to ensure your success in the course.

Please let me know a convenient time for you, and I will schedule the meeting accordingly. If you have any further concerns or questions, please do not hesitate to reach out to me.

Thank you for bringing this matter to my attention, and I look forward to working with you to find a solution.

• Withdrawal after the tenth week is only permitted for documented extenuating circumstances, and must be approved by the dean.

• Students can request to view their own recording within 30 days of the exam.

• If you suspect a compromise of your account, report it to the IT Service Desk within 24 hours to avoid account lockout.

• No courses can be added after the tenth day of the semester.
